channel.title: Ballot Book NZ — what changed
channel.description: New and changed 2026 election policies and candidates (from policy.nz), new opinion polls and party press releases, as picked up by Ballot Book NZ, an independent, non-partisan guide to the 7 November 2026 New Zealand general election. Every item links to its source.

item.title: Labour: new policy — Ensure new customers don't get a better deal than existing ones
item.description: This party would prevent customers from creating deals just for new customers while charging existing customers more. Power companies are already required to check if customers are on the best deal; this would be extended to phone… Source: https://www.labour.org.nz/news/release-labour-will-crack-down-on-unfair-charges-on-bills

item.title: Labour: new policy — Base advertised discounts on the normal price of a product
item.description: This party would base advertised discounts on the lowest price that product has been in the 30 days before a sale starts. Companies would be required to keep a record of their prices so that all claims can be checked. Ignoring this rule… Source: https://www.labour.org.nz/news/release-labour-will-crack-down-on-unfair-charges-on-bills

item.title: Labour: new policy — Affirm NZ's Paris agreement and methane targets
item.description: This party would make sure methane targets keep NZ on track to meet its international commitments, while backing farmers to reduce emissions. It would affirm the country's commitment to the Paris Agreement, and make sure forestry ETS… Source: https://www.labour.org.nz/media/xdfhgrlt/labour-policy-manifesto-2026.pdf

item.title: Labour: new policy — Support social workers and youth workers
item.description: This party would develop and long-term plan for recruiting, training and retaining social workers. It would support professional qualifications for youth workers and whānau navigators for young people with parents in prison. Source: https://www.labour.org.nz/media/xdfhgrlt/labour-policy-manifesto-2026.pdf

item.title: Labour: new policy — Support growth in the creative industries, especially game development
item.description: This party would expand the Game Development Sector Rebate and explore similar types of support elsewhere in the creative industries. It would protect industry training for the creative industries (games, films, TV etc.) with the… Source: https://www.labour.org.nz/media/xdfhgrlt/labour-policy-manifesto-2026.pdf

item.title: Labour: new policy — Stop planned LNG import terminal in Taranaki
item.description: This party would stop the proposed LNG import facility in Taranaki. Source: https://www.labour.org.nz/media/xdfhgrlt/labour-policy-manifesto-2026.pdf

item.title: Labour: new policy — Set up a $30m fund for community solar batteries
item.description: This party would establish a $30m fund for community batteries to store solar power. Community batteries will let more neighbourhoods share the benefits of locally generated power, including households without panels on their roofs.… Source: https://www.labour.org.nz/media/xdfhgrlt/labour-policy-manifesto-2026.pdf

item.title: Labour: new policy — Reinstate the ban on offshore oil and gas exploration
item.description: This party would reinstate the ban on offshore oil and gas exploration, and phase out low-and medium-heat coal boilers by 2037. It would also stop the proposed LNG import facility in Taranaki. Source: https://www.labour.org.nz/media/xdfhgrlt/labour-policy-manifesto-2026.pdf

item.title: Labour: new policy — Reassert Māori-led services and community care for Māori children and youth
item.description: This party would reinstate and strengthen Section 7AA so tamariki Māori and rangatahi remain connected to their family and identity. In partnership with Māori, it would create a 10-year plan to devolve care and protection services closer… Source: https://www.labour.org.nz/media/xdfhgrlt/labour-policy-manifesto-2026.pdf

item.title: Labour: new policy — Ratify the High Seas biodiversity treaty
item.description: This party would ratify the United Nations treaty on biodiversity in the high seas. If elected, this party would do this within its first 100 days in office. Source: https://www.labour.org.nz/media/xdfhgrlt/labour-policy-manifesto-2026.pdf

item.title: Labour: new policy — Make community refugee sponsorship additional to the annual refugee quota
item.description: This party would make the places available through community refugee sponsorship additional to the annual refugee quota and increase the quota over time. Source: https://www.labour.org.nz/media/xdfhgrlt/labour-policy-manifesto-2026.pdf

item.title: Labour: new policy — Increase protection in the Hauraki Gulf
item.description: This party would remove ring-net fishing rights in the Hauraki Gulf High Protection Areas. It would also investigate restricting trawling within the 100-metre contour with exceptions for specialty fisheries. It would fully ban bottom… Source: https://www.labour.org.nz/media/xdfhgrlt/labour-policy-manifesto-2026.pdf

item.title: Labour: new policy — Grow wood processing in NZ
item.description: This party would support the growth of wood processing industry in NZ, especially businesses that use the whole tree. Source: https://www.labour.org.nz/media/xdfhgrlt/labour-policy-manifesto-2026.pdf

item.title: Labour: new policy — Give Māori more autonomy over their education and require school boards to give effect to Te Tiriti
item.description: This party would require school boards to give effect to Te Tiriti, and enable greater Māori leadership over Māori education. This would include expanding kōhanga reo, puna reo, kura kaupapa Māori and kura-ā-iwi. Source: https://www.labour.org.nz/media/xdfhgrlt/labour-policy-manifesto-2026.pdf

item.title: Labour: new policy — Fund water storage and catchment groups in rural areas
item.description: This party would progress water storage funding for farmers. It would continue to support catchment groups, made up of farmers, Māori, local communities and environmental groups to discuss water issues, in particular river systems. Source: https://www.labour.org.nz/media/xdfhgrlt/labour-policy-manifesto-2026.pdf

item.title: Labour: new policy — Establish an independent redress system for survivors of abuse in state care
item.description: This party would create an independent redress system in line with the High Level Design Group's proposal. It would revisit findings on torture (beyond the Lake Alice findings) in care and amend the Limitations Act so that time limits… Source: https://www.labour.org.nz/media/xdfhgrlt/labour-policy-manifesto-2026.pdf

item.title: Labour: new policy — Establish a National Adaption Act so communities can plan for climate resilience
item.description: This party would pass a national Adaptation Act so communities, councils, Māori and government can plan together. It would work with banks and insurers on affordable finance to make homes more resilient, and prevent building in the… Source: https://www.labour.org.nz/media/xdfhgrlt/labour-policy-manifesto-2026.pdf

item.title: Labour: new policy — Ensure benefits and rent subsidies keep up with the cost of living
item.description: This party would make sure support doesn’t fall behind the cost of living. It would increase benefits by whichever is higher: inflation or average wage growth through indexation. It would reverse National’s changes to the Income-Related… Source: https://www.labour.org.nz/media/xdfhgrlt/labour-policy-manifesto-2026.pdf

item.title: Labour: new policy — Create additional support for asylum seekers and people fleeing humanitarian crises
item.description: This party would create a humanitarian visa for family members of New Zealanders in places of war and crisis. It would also give recognised refugees who arrived as asylum seekers the same support as other refugees and ave at least 15… Source: https://www.labour.org.nz/media/xdfhgrlt/labour-policy-manifesto-2026.pdf

item.title: Labour: new policy — Create a national memorial day for victims of abuse in state care
item.description: This party would create an annual memorial day for the public to learn about NZ's history of abuse, and ongoing issues of harm to vulnerable people. It would not be a statutory holiday. Source: https://www.labour.org.nz/media/xdfhgrlt/labour-policy-manifesto-2026.pdf

item.title: Labour: new policy — Aim to protect 30 percent of NZ's ocean areas
item.description: This party would aim to protect 30 percent of NZ's marine environment. It would ban seabed mining, prevent new areas of seamount from bottom trawling and reform marine protection law to include estuaries, wetlands and salt marshes. Source: https://www.labour.org.nz/media/xdfhgrlt/labour-policy-manifesto-2026.pdf
